statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-6575 (PostgreSQL pg_restore_attribute_stats accepts values that cause query planning to read past end of stats array) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.4: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6575/ lists 18.4 as the fixed release for major version 18. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/661095c40c0bcbb9c49743f518417a2977b63aef ('Fix MCV input array checks in statistics restore functions') on the REL_18_STABLE branch. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-6575 under its 18.4-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with that APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We checked every postgresql18 build published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64. In each, the postgres server reports the PostgreSQL release matching the package version. The message the fix adds to the server, 'could not parse "%s": incorrect number of elements (same as "%s" required)', is in /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres (postgresql18 package) of 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 and absent from 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0. 18.4-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 are affected.
